newsitem.title: THAILAND: Queen boosts British business in Thailand.
newsitem.headline: Queen boosts British business in Thailand.

text.p: Queen Elizabeth and her husband Prince Philip did their bit for British business in Thailand on Wednesday by visiting a trade fair and an exhibition on Anglo-Thai commercial links.

The queen, wearing a turquoise dress with blue and yellow flowers and a matching hat, stood in front of a couple of gleaming motorcyles to speak to the director of a bike distributor before inspecting other booths in the exhibition aimed at showcasing British products in Thailand.
A British businessman said trade between the countries was booming, with about one billion pounds ($1.61 billion) of British goods exported to Thailand in 1995.
Prince Philip traded quips with businessmen at the exhibition before moving on to a trade fair at a nearby shopping mall showing the various British retailers operating in Thailand.
Greeted with the sound of bagpipes, the prince spoke briefly with some models posing in front of a video showing scenes from Ascot before entering a makeshift British pub.
After declining a pint of Guinness beer with a laugh, the prince left to drive to the war cemetery in Kanchanaburi in western Thailand near the Burma border.
He laid a wreath at the Commonwealth War Graves Commission cemetery, which is filled with graves of soldiers who died building the infamous "Death Railway" between Burma and Thailand.
Queen Elizabeth and Prince Philip will continue their five-day visit to Thailand on Thursday with a visit to the northeastern province of Sakon Nakhon.
They are in Thailand to commemorate the 50th anniversary on the throne of King Bhumibol Adulyadej -- the world's longest reigning monarch.
